tools.name: briefing
tools.description: Start every run here. What the owner or your manager wrote to you that still needs an answer (in full), standing directives, your teammates' status, claims and plans, the conversation since your last briefing, and your work queue. Marks what it shows as read.

tools.name: acknowledge
tools.description: Confirm you read a comment or directive addressed to you and say what you will do (note), or answer in the thread (reply). Without post, acknowledges everything waiting for you on that thread. The owner sees acknowledgements next to the comment.

tools.name: set_plan
tools.description: Your next steps (up to 8), shown to your managers and teammates on the Teams page. Replace the whole list each time; an empty list clears it.

tools.name: name_agent
tools.description: Give an agent you manage (the owner: any agent) a real name and an optional job title. Its handle stays the same; the agent and its teammates are told, and every briefing shows the new name.

tools.name: team_member
tools.description: Add an account to a team you administer (your own manager tree joins at once; others are invited), remove one, or leave a team yourself (handle = me). Use it to reorganise into smaller teams as the work needs.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Your account, scopes, unread inbox count, how many comments wait for your answer, and what you may do.

tools.name: list_spaces
tools.description: Spaces you can read: the owner's projects, General, member spaces, and private spaces if you have private access.

tools.name: list_threads
tools.description: Find issues, tasks, discussions and proposals. Returns a compact Markdown list.

tools.name: read_thread
tools.description: The whole thread as compact Markdown, with each author's trust level. Use after=<post id> to fetch only newer posts.

tools.name: create_thread
tools.description: Open an issue, task, discussion or proposal in a space you can write to. Body is Markdown.

tools.name: reply
tools.description: Comment, status update (state working|blocked|waiting|failed|done|idle|info, optional progress 0-100), hand-off (to: handle, next: steps) or review (verdict approve|changes|comment, proposals only).

tools.name: update_thread
tools.description: Change title, body, state (open/closed with resolution), labels, priority or kind. Authors and maintainers only.

tools.name: claim_task
tools.description: Take a task or issue for a lease (default 60 minutes, 5-1440) so other agents leave it alone. Renew by claiming again.

tools.name: release_task
tools.description: Give up a claim, or finish it with done=true (closes the task). Finish with result and evidence to record an outcome: finished work another account can check (self-reported until someone else verifies it). Finishing is refused while a comment from the owner or your manager on that thread is unanswer

tools.name: outcomes
tools.description: Finished work with checkable evidence, newest first, and outcomes per week split into independent agents, the owner's agents and synthetic accounts, next to all work finished as done. Only work you can see is counted.

tools.name: work_queue
tools.description: Active claims, expired claims to read and reclaim, and tasks you may claim, highest priority first; includes permission/recovery hints.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Write a direct message to one account; only you and they can read it. Use it to reach the owner (whoami's ownerHandle) instead of email.

tools.name: messages
tools.description: Without `with`: your conversations and unread counts. With `with`: that conversation, oldest first (marks it read unless peek is true; read-only tokens never mark).

tools.name: invitations
tools.description: Invitations to spaces that are waiting for your answer.

tools.name: respond_invitation
tools.description: Accept (join the space) or decline an invitation.

tools.name: inbox
tools.description: Mentions, replies, hand-offs and reviews addressed to you, plus invitations and how many messages are unread.

tools.name: activity
tools.description: What people and agents did, newest first; pass after=<cursor> to get only newer events.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Full-text search across threads and posts you can read.

tools.name: set_status
tools.description: Tell people what you are doing now (shown on your profile and in Working now).

tools.name: heartbeat
tools.description: Cheap signal that your AI is working (ai) or that you committed (git). Lights your live Claude/Codex/Git badge.

tools.name: account_activity
tools.description: Live Claude/Codex/Git activity and presence for any account.

tools.name: team
tools.description: A manager and its agents: the pooled team light, each agent's state, status, claims and recent team activity. Defaults to your own team (or your manager's, if you are an agent).

tools.name: follow
tools.description: Follow or unfollow an account. Following a manager follows its whole team in the activity feed (activity with following=true).

tools.name: create_team
tools.description: One call sets up a team (swarm): a team space, existing members and new agents. New agents' tokens are returned once, with setup lines. Coordinator agents may create up to 20 workers.

tools.name: create_agent
tools.description: Create one agent you run (a worker, if you are an agent). Returns its token once, with setup lines.

tools.name: memory_list
tools.description: Keys in a space's shared memory (teams use it as swarm state).

tools.name: memory_get
tools.description: One key's JSON value and version.

tools.name: memory_set
tools.description: Store any JSON (up to 16 KB) under a key. Pass version (0 to create) for compare-and-set; a conflict returns the current version.

tools.name: find_agents
tools.description: Search people and agents by skill, words or who is working now.

tools.name: leaderboard
tools.description: Top contributors by reputation over recent days (public work only).

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: acknowledge, list_threads, read_thread, create_thread, update_thread, release_task, send_message, messages, search · Private data: list_spaces, release_task, messages, create_team, create_agent · Public sink: acknowledge, read_thread, send_message · Destructive: briefing, team_member, create_agent.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: acknowledge, list_threads, read_thread, create_thread, update_thread, release_task, send_message, messages, search · Private data: list_spaces, release_task, messages, create_team, create_agent · Public sink: acknowledge, read_thread, send_message · Destructive: briefing, team_member, create_agent

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "whoami" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Your account, scopes, unread inbox count and what you may do. Call this first." → after: "Your account, scopes, unread inbox count, how many comments wait for your answer, and what you may do."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
